title: Cust-managed key provisioning and audit-log SLA review - Northshore Consortium
next_steps: Redwood to share SOC 2 + ISO artifacts and HSM attestation checklist
Schedule 2-week BYOK POC with payload-limited keys (target start 2026-11-16)
Provide performance numbers for key unwrap latency under 1k/s and pricing delta for HSM-backed keys
action_items: Maya Chen - send SOC2/ISO pack and encryption whitepaper by 2026-11-06
Arjun Patel - draft proposed BYOK POC plan and test matrix by 2026-11-09
Lisa Morales - confirm governance owners and provide expected key rotation window by 2026-11-10
summary: Security-focused onboarding call to align on customer-managed keys (BYOK), HSM integration options, audit log retention/SLA, and operational tradeoffs for Northshore Consortium. Discussed key wrapping, escrow, rotation, attestation and performance implications. Agreed on a short BYOK POC and follow-up deliverables.
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for carving time, really appreciate it. We're here to map out how Northshore wants to run customer-managed keys with Redwood and make sure the audit log and residency pieces fit your compliance needs. Quick intros?
[00:17] Lisa Morales (Security Lead, Northshore): Yeah hi I'm Lisa, security lead. We own encryption policy and audits.
[00:23] Tom Becker (Platform Eng): Tom, platform engineering. I'll be the hands-on person for integration.
[00:29] Ravi Singh (Compliance): Ravi, compliance — SOC2/ISO owner.
[00:34] Nina Park (SRE): Nina, SRE, performance and runbooks.
[00:38] Maya Chen: Great. From Redwood, Arjun and Jules are here as well. Arjun will run through the HSM/BYOK options and Jules will cover audit logs and RBAC flows.
[00:47] Arjun Patel (Redwood SE): Thanks. Quick caveat up front — some of my terms may come out a little shorthand, and the auto-transcript may render H-S-M as H S M or 'hash em' occasionally, apologies.
[00:56] Lisa: No worries. We see mis-transcriptions a lot.
[01:03] Arjun: Alright, overview: Redwood supports three primary key models for customers wanting custody: 1) Cloud-KMS managed keys uploaded as customer-owned (BYOK) where the key material is in your cloud provider KMS, 2) HSM-backed keys via our HSM connectors (FIPS 140-2 level 3/4 style hardware), and 3) local on-prem key wrapping where you keep master key in your vault and we only store wrapped keys.
[01:36] Tom: For option 1, is Redwood making any copies of the key material?
[01:40] Arjun: Short answer: no plaintext copies. We only store wrapped key material — we integrate with cloud KMS to perform unwrap/operation calls, or with your HSM over a secure channel. There are two flow variants: direct KMS calls (Redwood calls your KMS) versus key escrow where you rotate a wrapped key blob and provide it to us.
[01:58] Nina: When you say 'call your KMS' what's the latency profile? We care about tail latency for generation use-cases.
[02:05] Arjun: Good question. There's a small extra RTT for unwrap operations. For typical clouds, unwrap is in the 5-15 ms range per call, but with HSM we see 10-40 ms depending on load and attestation. For streaming token generation we use a hybrid approach — we cache the derived data key in memory with strict TTLs and use prefix KV caching to avoid per-token unwraps.
[02:29] Nina: So you're caching keys in-process? How's that reconciled with our policy that no plaintext key leaves our KMS?
[02:36] Arjun: Right, that's the tradeoff. With option 2 (HSM-backed), we can perform cryptographic operations inside the HSM or proxied calls so the master key never lands in Redwood memory. For throughput-sensitive use, we use a derived ephemeral data key that is generated via KMS/HSM and kept in secure enclave on the serving node for the TTL — we can reduce TTLs and rotate aggressively. We can also offer a no-cache mode with performance penalty.
[03:02] Ravi: For audits we'll need full traceability — who called what, when, and which key wrapped/unwrapped. How do your audit logs capture KMS activity?
[03:11] Jules Rivera (Redwood SE): Our audit logs include per-request metadata: which API key/token requested model inference, associated customer key-id, whether a wrap/unwrap was performed, response codes, and region. We can push logs to your SIEM or S3 with signed delivery. Retention is configurable — default 90 days, enterprise can request 7 years as needed.
[03:33] Lisa: Can we get immutable logs? For regulatory reasons we need tamper-evident storage.
[03:38] Jules: Yes — we support WORM-style exports to an append-only S3 bucket with server-side object lock, and we can provide periodic signed manifests. We also support pushing to your Splunk/Elastic with signing headers.
[03:51] Tom: Who has access to key-related audit logs internally at Redwood? Need RBAC specifics.
[03:56] Maya: Great question — RBAC at Redwood is role-based and audited. Only the security ops role and the specific engineering on-call (with just-in-time elevation) can view raw key material traces — and we don't store plaintext keys. Access to key event logs can be scoped to your account and requires SSO with SAML and 2FA.
[04:14] Lisa: Is there support for SCIM groups to map our IAM roles to Redwood roles?
[04:18] Maya: Yep, we support SAML + SCIM provisioning and granular RBAC. You can map groups to roles: auditor, key-admin, engineer, read-only.
[04:26] Nina: About HSM attestation — do you support remote attestation? We need to verify HSM firmware and module state.
[04:33] Arjun: We integrate with vendor attestation APIs for AWS NitroTPM, Azure Confidential Compute attestation, and on-prem HSMs typically provide a signed attestation document (PKCS #7 style or vendor-specific). We can pass attestation up to your compliance team. For third-party HSMs we can arrange a joint audit.
[04:55] Ravi: What about key rotation and stale key destruction — chain of custody?
[04:59] Jules: Rotation is configurable. We support automated rotation schedules, manual rotation via API, and forced rotation as part of incident response. When a key is retired we 1) mark key-id as retired, 2) prevent new unwraps, 3) rotate in-flight caches, and 4) provide an exportable retention ledger for destroyed wrapped blobs. We can also support secure key escrow with an escrow broker if required by policy.
[05:26] Lisa: Escrow makes me nervous; what's your model? Is it an internal Redwood escrow?
[05:31] Arjun: We prefer the customer-managed escrow pattern: you maintain a second copy in your vault or an escrow partner. Redwood can sign the wrapped blob and approve rotation events but we do not hold plaintext copies by default. If a customer wants Redwood to hold an encrypted escrow, we can provide that under a separate agreement with stricter controls and mutual attestation.
[05:50] Tom: How do you verify key provenance during forensics? E.g., if we see an unexpected unwrap, how do we prove the call originated from our org?
[05:58] Jules: Each unwrap or cryptographic operation produces an event with a signed digest referring to the request id, originating API token, source IP, and the KMS key-id. We can feed those signed digests back to you and include certificate chain data for the HSM attestation.
[06:16] Lisa: Do you support split-key or threshold cryptography if we want to avoid a single custodian?
[06:21] Arjun: We have an experimental flow for multi-party keys using threshold schemes. It's more complex operationally and increases latency, but it's doable — we can include it in the POC if you want.
[06:33] Nina: On residency: can we keep keys strictly in eu-west-1 and disallow any cross-region replication?
[06:39] Maya: Yes, regional confinement is supported. For Hosted mode we pin KMS calls to your regional KMS endpoint. For Dedicated or Private deployments you can configure region-only routing and we will disable cross-region fallbacks.
[06:53] Ravi: About SOC 2 evidence — we will need control descriptions of key management and redundancy. Do you have template evidence?
[06:59] Maya: We'll share our SOC 2 and ISO docs and our key management control narrative. I'll attach the control mapping table against your control IDs.
[07:07] Lisa: Can Redwood sign the control narrative with a notarized attestation for our auditors?
[07:12] Maya: We can provide signed statements and auditor contact, yes — subject to NDA and your audit process.
[07:18] Tom: A practical ops question — how is cache eviction handled when a key is rotated? We don't want stale decrypted keys in RAM.
[07:25] Arjun: We implement a rotate-and-revoke pattern — when rotation occurs we push a revocation event that triggers immediate in-memory TTL expiry and a short grace period for in-flight requests. We can tune grace windows. Also we support hardened memory erasure on node-level: mlock and explicit zeroization when TTLs end.
[07:46] Nina: If we do HSM-backed keys, what's the throughput profile? We need target 5k unwraps/sec for batched workloads in peak windows.
[07:55] Arjun: Single HSM often caps around a few hundred ops/sec depending on algorithm. To reach 5k/s you need a pool of HSMs or use an architecture where you use HSM to derive a high-entropy data key then cache the data key across serving nodes. For streaming we avoid per-token unwrapping; we unwrap per-session. We'll provide numbers in the test plan.
[08:17] Lisa: What about the crypto algorithms? Are there limits?
[08:20] Jules: We support RSA 3072/4096, ECDSA P-256/P-384, and AES-256-GCM for data keys. We also support key wrapping via RFC 3394/AES-KW and KMIP where applicable. If you have FIPS or algorithm constraints we can comply.
[08:36] Ravi: For key deletion we need verifiable destruction — can you run secure erase and provide attestation?
[08:41] Arjun: For wrapped blobs in Redwood storage we can provide an erasure log and signed deletion receipts. For keys in your KMS/HSM, you'd provide the destruction evidence from your provider. For our managed escrow, we can provide a signed destruction statement.
[08:58] Tom: Regarding SSO mapping, can we restrict unwrap operations to specific service accounts only?
[09:04] Maya: Yes, policy can be scoped to service principal or service account. You can also require MFA/just-in-time for human-triggered unwraps.
[09:13] Nina: Is there a way to force re-attestation of HSM hardware periodically?
[09:17] Arjun: Yes, we can schedule periodic attestation checks and surface any drift. We can also automate quarterly firmware checks as part of the POC.
[09:26] Lisa: One more compliance ask — we need a retention SLA for audit logs and a guaranteed export window in case of legal hold.
[09:33] Jules: We can commit to export within 24 hours for legal hold requests and provide a preservation copy to your legal bucket. SLA and retention length are contract-negotiable.
[09:45] Ravi: On threat modeling — if a Redwood node is compromised, what prevents exfiltration of data keys?
[09:52] Arjun: Defense-in-depth: keys are encrypted at rest, master keys remain in your KMS/HSM when BYOK is used; we rely on ephemeral data keys with tight TTLs and mlock/zeroization. We also have process-level sandboxing, hardware-backed enclaves available in private deployments, and network controls to limit admin access.
[10:12] Lisa: Do you have an incident playbook for key compromise?
[10:16] Maya: Yes — it includes immediate key revocation, rotation, notifying customers, forensic collection, and coordinating escrow recovery. We'll share the runbook subset that's safe for customers.
[10:26] Tom: Let's talk about cost. HSM-backed keys are more expensive — how do you bill unwraps or HSM ops?
[10:32] Maya: We bill BYOK/HSM as a priced add-on: there's a per-request premium (to reflect HSM op cost) and a monthly subscription for reserved HSM pool capacity if you want throughput SLAs. We'll provide the pricing tiers in the follow-up.
[10:46] Nina: In Dedicated deployment if we run in our VPC with your private control plane, can we still force keys never to transit Redwood-managed networks?
[10:54] Arjun: With Private deployment, the control plane can sit in your VPC and all KMS traffic can be internal-only — we can architect for zero-hops across public internet. That meets strict data residency and egress requirements.
[11:06] Lisa: Are there any cryptographic operations that require your root/key material to ever be reconstituted?
[11:11] Jules: No for BYOK we never request plaintext. For some legacy workflows we may have to do wrap/unwrap cycles but these are all via KMS/HSM APIs. If a customer elects Redwood-managed keys, then Redwood holds the master but with strict controls and SCM audits.
[11:25] Ravi: For our auditors, they'd like a short test: we want to see a signed unwrap event and the attestation chain for the HSM provider. Can you provide that during the POC?
[11:33] Maya: Absolutely, that's what we'll include in the test plan.
[11:36] Tom: We use an internal key rotation cadence of 30 days for some PI keys. Can your rotation frequency be shortened?
[11:42] Arjun: Yes you can have daily rotation if you want; the operational cost increases but it's supported. We'll capture the exact cadence in the POC matrix.
[11:51] Lisa: We need to discuss key labeling and metadata — our auditors demand an immutable lineage tag per key with policy references.
[11:58] Jules: We attach metadata to each key-id and it is part of the signed digest. We can provide an export of the lineage as a CSV or machine-readable manifest.
[12:09] Nina: Slightly off topic: what's your approach to multi-tenancy — will our keys ever be co-located on the same HSM as other customers?
[12:16] Arjun: Multi-tenancy depends on model. For hosted shared pools, wrapped blobs from multiple tenants may be on the same storage nodes but keys are namespaced and access-controlled. For HSM we can provide dedicated partitions or dedicated HSMs depending on the contract.
[12:29] Lisa: Could you do a sketch of high-level flows for the POC?
[12:34] Maya: Sure, high level POC plan: 1) baseline: Redwood-managed keys for functional test, 2) BYOK cloud KMS flow: Redwood calls your KMS to unwrap/derive data keys; 3) HSM flow: connect to your HSM or our dedicated HSM test instance with attestation; 4) performance & audit tests: per-second unwraps, log export, tamper-evidence checks.
[12:58] Tom: For step 3, if we bring our on-prem HSM behind a VPN, what's the recommended network pattern?
[13:04] Arjun: We recommend an IPSec or private interconnect and a small NAT ingress only for the attestation and control plane. Data plane traffic for inference stays in your VPC if Private mode is used.
[13:16] Nina: Any gotchas for key-type conversion? We have some legacy RSA keys.
[13:20] Jules: Noted — we can support RSA wrap but modern recommendations are ECC/AES. We'll include a migration path that does automated re-wrapping with your consent.
[13:31] Lisa: Could Redwood run a 'red-team' style simulation internally to prove no key exfil?
[13:36] Maya: We run internal pen tests and third-party tests. For an explicit simulation against your tenancy we'd need a scoped engagement and mutual authorization.
[13:46] Ravi: What about legal process — subpoenas for keys or access requests?
[13:51] Maya: As with any provider, we respond to lawful process. With BYOK where keys are in your control, Redwood cannot decrypt data without your cooperation. We'll include the legal process section in the contract terms.
[14:03] Tom: For the POC, what logs and metrics will you surface to our SREs?
[14:08] Jules: We'll expose metrics for unwrap latency, unwrap ops/sec per key-id, cache hit rate, key rotation events, and audit log push status. We'll also provide trace IDs for cross-correlation.
[14:20] Nina: Is sampling applied to logs? We want full fidelity for security events.
[14:24] Jules: By default security events are not sampled; high-volume telemetry may be sampled at 1% for cost metrics but audit logs are always full-fidelity.
[14:35] Lisa: One more — are there integration examples with Thales/Entrust HSMs?
[14:40] Arjun: Yes, we've integrated with Thales Luna, Utimaco, and Azure Key Vault HSMs. We'll include connector configs.
[14:48] Tom: Ok, let's capture immediate deliverables.
[14:51] Maya: Action items: Maya to share SOC2/ISO artifacts and the key-management control narrative; Arjun to produce BYOK POC plan and test matrix; Jules to provide log-export and attestation examples; Lisa will confirm internal governance owners and key rotation windows. Anything else?
[15:06] Lisa: Please include estimated cost delta for HSM mid-tier and the throughput numbers.
[15:10] Maya: Noted, we'll include pricing in the next email.
[15:14] Ravi: Can we also get a short security FAQ tailored to auditors?
[15:18] Maya: Yes — a one-pager for auditors.
[15:21] Nina: And runbook snippets for rotation and compromise response.
[15:24] Maya: We'll include those.
[15:27] Tom: Great. Unless anyone has more questions, we'll wrap.
[15:30] Lisa: No more from me. Thanks.
[15:33] Maya: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the pack and a calendar invite for the POC kickoff.
[15:38] (call ends)

Notes on transcript quality: occasional mislabeling, audio had a small echo at 00:50 causing a couple words to garble.
